annotationRationale: The central skill is relating a mean change to a total-score change. The two-variable system and the one-variable excess-point model are useful distinct routes, so their equation-solving concepts remain method-specific. The historical single-variable-mean route is a substitution variant of the system rather than an additional method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Prealgebra is reasonable for this elementary mean and equation-modeling problem. No obvious area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The conditions uniquely give a current mean of 7 over 3 quizzes. A total of 21 becomes 32/4=8 or 54/6=9 in the two scenarios, confirming choice D. No stem, choice, figure or grading contradiction appears.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: 2023_AMC_10A_Q10/mean-total-system and 2023_AMC_10A_Q10/excess-points-above-mean were independently verified and retained. 2023_AMC_10A_Q10/single-variable-mean has only a historical route label, with no worked explanation; its proposed substitution approach is reasonably merged into the equivalent system route. The other supplied AoPS algebraic and answer-testing variants do not require another method.
review.annotationCheck: Mean is appropriately the question-level assessed concept. System modeling/elimination and one-variable modeling/expansion are accurately retained as method-specific concepts.
review.areaCheck: Prealgebra is reasonable for this elementary mean and equation-modeling problem. No obvious area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The two mean equations simplify correctly to m+n=10 and 3m+2n=27. Subtracting twice the first from the second gives m=7 and consequently n=3, a valid quiz count.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Faithfully reuses 2023_AMC_10A_Q10/mean-total-system. Both inherited LIVE and AoPS reference IDs are preserved, and the current-question references also support the route. Reuse of the credited project prose is consistent with the packet; no official MAA authorship is claimed.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The total equals mean times count motivation is explicit. Both scenarios use the same original total, and the cancellations and elimination are shown sufficiently for a learner to reproduce them.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_211 matches mean-total reasoning, cnm_091 matches the two-unknown contextual model, and cnm_090 matches the displayed subtraction elimination.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: All three exact native-topic links match the method.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.EE.C.8c directly fits the contextual linear system. Other supplied system links support equation creation and algebraic solution, without establishing graphing or an elimination-equivalence proof. The 6.SP links support the mean component only, not spread or distribution shape; some supplied rationales mention content beyond this standalone mean node.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The three immediate nodes are precise, with mean central and the system concepts specific to this route.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Existing deviations from the old mean sum to zero. One new 11 therefore contributes n+1 excess points; three contribute 3(n+1), which must equal 2(n+3). This gives n=3 and old mean 11-4=7.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly retains 2023_AMC_10A_Q10/excess-points-above-mean and its inherited aops-reference-2023_AMC_10A_Q10 credit. The current AoPS Solution 5 supports the same argument. The project reuse and third-party-informed basis are accurately identified.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why only the new scores contribute excess. It clearly distinguishes excess relative to the old mean from the new mean, making the key equation understandable without an unfamiliar prerequisite.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_211 captures the balancing interpretation of mean, cnm_045 the one-variable contextual equation, and cnm_043 its parenthesized expansion and solution.
